purpose: Retain a verified per-lesson original V1 A-D review trace during whole-unaccepted-cohort Stage A; not academic approval
title: Choose Objects to Compare Length Indirectly

sourceBasis.note: Previously registered SHA values reused; no new SHA computed or publisher figures licensed/redistributed.

stageA.warmup: Compare A and C pencil lengths indirectly from reference B and explain the relation; source visual not independently cleared.
stageA.activity1: Mai and Clare Walk to School: determine the shorter path using one movable third comparison tool (string/connecting-cube tower/pencil); student independently explains method; original map's exact graphics not independently cleared.

activity2.name: Will It Fit?
originalStudentFacingQuestions: Will the teacher's desk fit through the door?
Will a student desk fit through the door?
Which is longer, the bookshelf or the rug?
Which is longer, the file cabinet or the bookshelf?
Which is shorter, the bookshelf or the teacher's desk?
Will the teacher's desk fit next to the bookshelf?
activity2.response: For EACH of six prompts, show drawings, numbers or words; choose and explain third-object tool; correctly distinguish WIDTH from length and door opening; not automatically inferred from simulated numbers.

stageA.lessonSynthesis: Compare objects that cannot be lined up by using a movable intermediary object; classroom choices and genuine measuring remain teacher supervised.

stageB.remaining: Compare all six original Student Facing prompts with actual effective Rich V2; do not assert a digital numeric example substitutes live classroom measurement.

stageC.teacherOnlyBoundary: Real pupil-selected tool, measured furniture/doors, explanation drawings and source figures cannot be scored as completed by numeric Practice.

nextAction: Preserve the existing source-specific digital practice and teacher-oriented lesson candidate; complete source-vs-effective-render parity for all currently unaccepted lessons in the Stage A cohort, then prepare scoped B/C repairs before full-grade freeze and CI.
